title: 20-Year Treasury Bond auction (November new issue) — the quarterly new-issue slot, sized by the 11-12 announcement
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream. Row reads verbatim `20-Year BOND / Announcement Thursday, November 12, 2026 / Auction Wednesday, November 18, 2026 / Settlement Monday, November 30, 2026` — the ABSENCE of Treasury's trailing `R` reopening marker is what makes this a NEW ISSUE. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-12 initial research (2026-09-08). It is one of the two auctions that announcement exists to size, which is why it is filed rather than merely noted. THE NEW-ISSUE CADENCE, verified rather than assumed: fiscaldata auctions_query (pulled 2026-09-08, all 20-Year rows since 2023-01-01, n=44) shows the 20Y running a Feb/May/Aug/Nov new-issue cycle with two intervening reopenings — 2023-11-20, 2024-11-20, 2025-11-19 were all November new issues, so 2026-11-18 is the fourth consecutive one. EXPECTED SIZE $16B, and this is the strongest base rate in the nominal complex: 13 consecutive new issues at $16B since 2023-08-23, 29 reopenings at $13B over the same run, 37 -> now 44 auctions in the window with ZERO deviations across three years and an 82bp range in the 10Y. The number is NOT published today — sb0590's anticipated-size table ends at Oct-26 — and becomes published on 2026-11-04, eight days before the announcement that reads it. A print off $16B would mean the 2026-11-04 refunding moved the grid, which would be the first nominal coupon size change since April 2024 (fiscaldata, same pull: last increases 2026-04-24 5Y 67 -> 70 and 2024-04-25 7Y 43 -> 44). PREDECESSOR CUSIP for the pricing comparison: 912810UX4, the August 2026 new issue, sold 2026-08-19 at $16B, high yield 5.204%, bid-to-cover 2.53; its second reopening is treasury-20y-bond-2026-10-21, already tracked. Settlement is 2026-11-30 rather than the usual mid-month date because the November new issue settles at month end. Proposed as an estimate; symbols: [] and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
